system: Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. Property-only voice, music-style, beat and sound-texture references condition a new sound; they do not play the original recording. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: The complete supplied character reference sheet remains one intact, continuously visible image, framed exactly as provided and filling the target frame without cropping, rearranging, or extracting any single panel. The composition keeps its stacked structure: a wide cinematic hero view across the top, a middle row of full-body turnaround views, and a lower row of close-up detail studies, with the dark neutral studio backdrop and the rain-slick rooftop setting held in their original spatial relationships. The adult character in black tactical gear stays at the center of attention, with short dark hair, a high-collared jacket, cargo trousers, and lace-up combat boots reading clearly at every scale.Low-key, high-contrast light shapes the sheet: cool blue-gray ambience and warm amber practicals glow behind the hero figure, while soft directional studio light rakes across the turnaround panels and reveals the matte fabric, straps, buckles, and leather of the boots. In the hero view, the figure stands upright with arms relaxed at the sides, head turned slightly to the side; in the turnaround row, frontal, profile, and back views hold their measured spacing; in the detail row, the face, collar, hands, and boots remain crisp, evenly lit studies. Fine rain streaks drift down through the upper image; distant city lights pulse and soften into bokeh; a thin sheen of water slides along the metal railing.The character's posture stays stable, but a faint breath subtly lifts the shoulders and shifts the jacket collar, giving the still image a restrained sense of life. The existing panel lettering and labels remain fully legible and exactly in place, and no new typography, panel, character, or location is introduced. The palette of near-black, charcoal, slate blue, cool gray, and warm amber remains unchanged, with the cool shadows and warm highlights preserved. Motion is continuous and gentle rather than eventful: rain keeps falling, light shimmers, water creeps along the railing, and the figure breathes, while the full reference-sheet presentation holds steady and unbroken for the entire duration.The image's own boundaries and internal borders stay fixed, so the eye can move from the widescreen hero image to the smaller turnaround and detail studies without any re-layout. The metal railing occupies the foreground plane in the hero section, with the city beyond falling into soft, layered bokeh; the character's silhouette remains dark and clean against those lights. The jacket's high collar sits close to the jaw, the straps and buckles catch small highlights, the cargo trousers break over the boots, and the laced footwear reads with a dull leather sheen. In the neutral reference panels, the figure's slim athletic build and short undercut with a small topknot remain legible from front, side, and back, while the close-up panels preserve the scar through one eyebrow, the texture of the collar, the relaxed hands, and the sturdy boots. The rain and city shimmer are restrained, never overtaking the sheet, and the warm amber points of light stay balanced against the cool blue-gray shadows. The overall effect is a quiet, breathing animatic of the original reference sheet rather than a newly staged scene.
